# Semidynamics and Nokia Explore Collaboration to Strengthen Europe’s Sovereign AI Capabilities

## Companies bring together Semidynamics’ AI accelerators and Nokia’s data center networking expertise to support European AI ambitions

Barcelona, Spain and Espoo, Finland — 29th October 2026— Semidynamics and Nokia have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to explore how their AI computing and data center networking technologies could support Europe’s sovereign AI ambitions. The companies will assess how their complementary technologies could work together in large-scale AI infrastructure and explore additional options for organizations building AI infrastructure.

The collaboration will explore opportunities to assess, test, validate and, where appropriate, integrate Semidynamics’ AI accelerators and liquid cooled racks with Nokia’s Data Center Fabric solutions. As part of this work, Semidynamics will evaluate Nokia’s networking technologies and related solutions for its AI inference racks.

Semidynamics is developing proprietary RISC-V-based AI inference technology and integrated systems, while Nokia provides the AI-optimized networking solutions that connect computing systems within data centers. Their shared objective is to strengthen Europe’s capacity to develop and deploy AI infrastructure using European technology. This work will help assess the feasibility of integrated solutions and inform potential joint technical and commercial propositions. For organizations developing sovereign AI infrastructure, the intended value is a broader base of technology expertise and potential options for future deployments.

“Europe’s AI ambitions need European technology that can be deployed at scale,” said Roger Espasa, CEO of Semidynamics. “Working with Nokia gives us a framework to advance our memory-centric inference platform alongside the networking needed for large AI infrastructure. Our aim is to give customers a stronger European technology offering for deploying AI at scale.”

“Strengthening Europe's AI capabilities means contributing technology and expertise to advance a broader, open ecosystem for trusted AI infrastructure,” said Matthieu Bourguignon, Senior Vice-President for Network Infrastructure Europe at Nokia. “Through this agreement, we will explore how computing and connectivity can work together to support organizations developing sovereign AI infrastructure with trusted technologies.”

### About Nokia

Nokia is a global leader in connectivity infrastructure, enabling the AI supercycle. We build networks that connect intelligence and deliver a comprehensive connectivity solution across fixed, mobile, IP, optical, core, and data center networks. With security by design, AI-driven innovation, and AI-optimized architecture, Nokia delivers trusted infrastructure that enables AI to scale and advances connectivity to secure a brighter world.

### About Semidynamics

Headquartered in Barcelona, Semidynamics is an advanced computing company developing memory-centric AI infrastructure. With a team of more than 200 engineers and specialists, the company designs proprietary silicon architectures and vertically integrated systems optimized for large-scale AI inference workloads. Semidynamics serves a global ecosystem of partners and customers and operates in compliance with applicable export controls and international trade regulations.

# Fireworks and Era4 partner to bring open-model AI to enterprises across the UK and Europe

Fireworks and Era4 have announced a partnership to help enterprises across the UK and Europe run and adapt open AI models on UK infrastructure. Under a multi-year agreement, Fireworks has contracted Era4’s entire Chesterfield facility in Derbyshire, comprising 5 MW of direct liquid-cooled capacity with NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra HGX B300 GPUs.

The partnership combines Fireworks’ model training and inference platform with infrastructure owned and operated by Era4 in the UK. The companies will initially explore joint solutions for financial services, insurance and life sciences.

“Companies want AI they can specialise to their own data and the way they work,” said Lin Qiao, co-founder and CEO of Fireworks. “They also want a choice about where those models run. This agreement with Era4 expands our capacity in the UK for developing new services with for banks, fintechs, UK enterprises, and other regulated businesses.”

Fireworks serves more than 40 trillion tokens a day, with over 95% of that volume coming from models specialised on customers’ own data. This new UK capacity comes as Fireworks expands its UK office, adding to a footprint that already includes deployment regions in Germany and Iceland.

For the proposed enterprise services, the companies will explore:

- UK-hosted inference, with on-demand and dedicated access to open models through Fireworks on Era4 infrastructure.
- Fine-tuning and serving models on enterprise data for uses such as underwriting, financial-crime checks, claims handling and software engineering.
- Joint customer deployments and reference architectures in the UK and Europe.

“Europe has the talent, the data and the demand to lead in enterprise AI, but it cannot lead on compute it does not control. For a bank or insurer, knowing where its AI runs is part of the buying decision,” said Tom Humphreys, CEO of Era4. “At Chesterfield, we own and operate the infrastructure, including behind-the-meter power generation. Working with Fireworks lets us build on that foundation with tools enterprises can use to adapt and run open models.”

“Enterprises across the UK and Europe are moving from AI experimentation to production, and they need the compute, the data sovereignty, and the model flexibility to do that at scale,” said Rod Evans, EMEA Vice President for Supercomputing and AI Cloud Infrastructure. “Fireworks and Era4 are bringing all three together on NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra infrastructure – giving regulated industries a path to deploy specialised AI models in UK-owned, UK-operated facilities. That’s exactly the kind of foundation that lets enterprises move AI into the services their customers depend on.”

Chesterfield uses direct liquid-cooled HPE ProLiant Compute XD685 servers in an HPE AI Mod POD modular data centre. Most of its electricity comes from landfill gas captured and used to generate power on site, with a grid connection as backup. Generating their own power means Era4 has been able to deploy infrastructure at Chesterfield quickly, bypassing grid constraints.

Alongside Chesterfield, Era4 has a portfolio of more than 40 sites across the UK with similar potential for energy generation, providing a clear pathway for future expansion.

## Naver Signs AI Infrastructure Deal with Brookfield… Meets Precondition for NVIDIA Investment

Brookfield to Invest Up to $9 Billion to Secure GPU Infrastructure Naver Cloud Launches AI Factory… Alleviating the Burden of Initial Investment NVIDIA Accelerates Completion of Procedures for $1 Billion Equity Investment Naver Also Decides on Payment Guarantees Totaling 18.74 Trillion Won

[E-Daily Reporter Lee So-Hyun ] Naver (NAVER(035420)) has signed a $9 billion agreement with global alternative investment firm Brookfield to secure artificial intelligence (AI) computing infrastructure. With this, the conditions precedent for NVIDIA’s $1 billion strategic equity investment have been met, and the 1-gigawatt (GW) global AI factory project—jointly pursued by Naver, NVIDIA, and Brookfield—has entered the full-scale implementation phase.

On the 27th, Naver announced in an amended disclosure regarding its “Future Business and Management Plans” that it had finalized a computing infrastructure agreement with Brookfield. Previously, Brookfield had been designated as the exclusive preferred negotiating party for 12 weeks to discuss a formal contract; however, this agreement has now established a concrete investment and operational structure.

Under the agreement, Brookfield will establish a special purpose vehicle (SPV) called “Asset Co. (tentative name)” and invest up to $9 billion to secure AI infrastructure, including graphics processing units (GPUs) and data centers. Naver Cloud will procure GPU-based computing resources from Asset Co. as a service (GPUaaS) to provide AI data center services to external customers.

Naver will lead the AI Factory business based on its capabilities in building and operating its own GPU clusters and its expertise in data center operations. NVIDIA plans to enhance infrastructure operational efficiency and competitiveness by providing technical cooperation centered on “DSX,” its next-generation high-performance computing platform.

Naver expects this partnership to alleviate the initial investment burden associated with building large-scale AI infrastructure. Brookfield will provide funding to secure the infrastructure, and Naver Cloud will pay usage fees tied to business revenue. Through this arrangement, the company aims to manage the financial burden during the early stages of the business while gradually expanding the infrastructure to meet AI computing demand.

Although a Brookfield-affiliated special purpose vehicle holds 100% of the equity in Asset, Naver’s control is recognized under Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS), and Asset is scheduled to be consolidated as a subsidiary.

This agreement is also expected to accelerate NVIDIA’s strategic equity investment in Naver. NVIDIA has agreed to participate in Naver’s third-party private placement, valued at approximately $1 billion. Since the investment’s preconditions have been met through this agreement, Naver plans to finalize the private placement process promptly and will provide further details at a later date.

AI Factory will begin operations in the first half of 2027 with a capacity of 55 megawatts (MW), using the hyperscale data center “Gak Sejong” as its core hub. It plans to increase capacity to 100 MW by the end of that year and to 200 MW by 2028. Long-term goals include building 1 GW-class infrastructure and expanding operations beyond the Asia-Pacific region into overseas markets such as Europe and the Middle East.

Meanwhile, Naver announced in a separate disclosure that day that it had decided to provide a debt guarantee worth 18.74 trillion won regarding Naver Cloud’s obligations to pay fees related to the AI Factory. This amount represents 64.73% of Naver’s equity.

This amount represents the total nominal value of GPU service fees expected to be paid through the end of 2034—the maximum contract term—assuming the full $9 billion investment limit is utilized. As of the date of the disclosure, there is no confirmed obligation to pay these fees, and the actual payment amount may vary depending on the GPU investment schedule, interest rates, and exchange rates.

Naver explained that this payment guarantee is a measure to build trust for the smooth execution of the contract, and that the guarantee itself does not immediately result in actual cash outflows or cost burdens.

Brookfield Capital, NVIDIA Technology, Naver Operations… Three-Party Alliance Gets Underway

The business structure involves Brookfield raising capital, NVIDIA providing technology, and Naver leading operations. Brookfield will establish an asset-holding company, “Asset Co. (tentative name),” through a special purpose vehicle (SPV) and invest up to $9 billion to secure AI infrastructure, including graphics processing units (GPUs) and data centers.

Naver Cloud will receive GPU-based computing resources from Asset Co. as a service (GPUaaS) to provide AI data center services to external customers. Naver will leverage its experience in building and operating its own GPU clusters and its data center operational expertise, while NVIDIA will provide technical collaboration centered on “DSX,” a next-generation high-performance computing platform.

Naver emphasizes that this partnership allows it to enter the AI infrastructure business while reducing the initial investment burden. Brookfield will provide the substantial capital required to build data centers and purchase GPUs, and Naver Cloud will pay usage fees tied to business revenue. GPU investments will also be made in phases to align with customer demand.

Overinvestment Sparked by CoreWeave… Naver Emphasizes Diversifying Financial Burden

This approach is drawing attention amid concerns over financial burdens in the global AI infrastructure industry. Recently, the financing risks faced by neo-cloud companies—which rely on large-scale capital expenditures and borrowing—have come to the fore, as evidenced by the yield on corporate bonds issued by U.S. AI cloud firm CoreWeave briefly surging to 15%.

Naver’s strategy is to leverage Brookfield’s capital-raising capabilities to spread the burden of direct capital expenditures. Brookfield manages over $1 trillion in assets worldwide and has extensive experience in large-scale infrastructure investments, such as establishing a semiconductor factory joint venture with Intel and collaborating with Microsoft on energy development.

In a report released on the 19th, Shinhan Investment Securities also assessed that Naver’s AI Factory business model involves leveraging external capital to share the burden of capital expenditures, thereby allowing the company to focus on acquiring customers and monetizing operations.

The fact that Naver has a stable cash flow base from its existing businesses—such as search, advertising, and commerce—is also cited as a key differentiator from NeoCloud companies, whose revenue is heavily concentrated on GPU rentals. The plan is to secure AI infrastructure as a new growth engine while maintaining the revenue base of its existing platform businesses.

Naver plans to build an AI factory with a capacity of 55 megawatts (MW) in the first half of 2027, reaching a cumulative 100 MW by the end of that year and a cumulative 200 MW by 2028, with the hyperscale data center “Gak Sejong” serving as its first hub. The long-term goal is to expand to a 1-gigawatt (GW) scale and extend the business beyond the Asia-Pacific region to overseas markets such as Europe and the Middle East.

However, this business structure also entails financial liabilities. In a separate disclosure issued today, Naver announced that it has decided to provide a debt guarantee of 18.74 trillion won for Naver Cloud’s payment obligations related to the AI Factory. This amount represents 64.73% of Naver’s equity.

This represents the total nominal amount of GPU service payments expected to be made by the end of 2034, assuming the full $9 billion investment limit is utilized. Currently, there are no confirmed payment obligations, and the actual amount may vary depending on the GPU investment schedule, interest rates, and exchange rates. The asset, which is 100% owned by Brookfield, is also expected to be consolidated as a subsidiary under Naver’s control in accordance with accounting standards.

A Naver spokesperson stated, “By combining the AI technology and data center operational capabilities we have accumulated over the years with NVIDIA’s cutting-edge computing platform capabilities and Brookfield’s global infrastructure investment capabilities, we have been able to secure both business stability and competitiveness,” adding, “Based on a capital-efficient business structure, we will create new growth opportunities in the global AI infrastructure market.”
